description: A read-only per-chip ARC telemetry sidecar for the qwen-c2-serving card steps (job key C2_TELEMETRY=1, interval C2_TELEMETRY_MS): AICLK and the limiter holding it, VCORE, chip and board power, TDC, ASIC and GDDR temperature, kernel NOP counters, fan, once a second for the whole smoke or gate step, a CSV and a per-chip summary line in the results. It reads the table the ARC firmware publishes with AXI reads (luwen's Blackhole get_telemetry(), the read tt-smi makes) and sends no ARC message. It is not a lever: no flag, no profile twin, no image file (it runs on the host from the checkout).
card_jobs: scripts/ci/references/fusion-jobs/TEL (TEL1: the solo prefill ladder prefill_ladder_solo on the production profile, TEL2: concurrent8_steady, both C2_TELEMETRY=1; ORDER.txt there)
notes: WP0 TODO. (1) tests: test_card_telemetry is the only thing this manifest asks WP0 to place (the CPU allowlist); make_fusion_profiles.py --write adds it, and until then the two 'checked-in files are what the manifests generate' tests (test_fusion_wp, test_tp4_fusion_jobs) are red by exactly that block. (2) TEL1 names the smoke test prefill_ladder_solo, which tp4/fusion-1 does not have: it is commit ebfe41ae of tp4/prefill-1 (c2_serving_smoke.py, c2_smoke_check.py's PREFILL_LADDER_TESTS rule, prefill_ladder_report.py). The smoke client and the smoke check run from the checkout on the host, so merging it into the tagged commit needs no image rebuild; without it TEL1 runs only the warm-up. (3) Nothing for the image: card_telemetry.py and card_telemetry.sh run on the host (the workflow steps source scripts/ci/card_telemetry.sh), so no image_files and no overlay line. (4) Shared files this branch DID edit, because the sidecar is wired into them and the preamble's shared list does not name them: .github/workflows/qwen-c2-serving.yml (the smoke and gate steps start and stop the sampler, plus one always-run summary step before the upload) and scripts/ci/c2_serving_job.py (the C2_TELEMETRY and C2_TELEMETRY_MS keys and outputs); expect a textual merge with other packages' edits of the same files, no semantic conflict. (5) 13x10: nothing depends on the compute grid; the sidecar reads the ARC, not the Tensix array. The firmware's fmax (AICLK_LIMIT_MAX) is read from the chip, never assumed.
